headline: High: shared MCP and overlapping file/network surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK exposes MCP and browser/web inputs, while Khoj ingests indexed documents and supports web search/RAG. That creates a plausible path where TREK content is fed into Khoj as trusted text, or vice versa, even though no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF TREK content is copied into Khoj notes or search inputs without provenance labels, prompt injection is possible.
IF either agent renders the other's retrieved text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted TREK outputs into Khoj indexes.
Add provenance labels to imported text and strip instructions from retrieved snippets.
Use a manual review step before any MCP-fed content is acted on.
Restrict TREK MCP tools to read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: add content-safety filtering between TREK exports and Khoj retrieval.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj reads personal notes/files and has broad network egress; TREK stores reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets in local files and logs. If the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive travel data can flow into Khoj outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared OS workspace, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF TREK uploads or exports reservations, API keys, or MFA secrets into a shared folder, Khoj can index them.
IF Khoj sends retrieved note contents to external search providers, copied TREK data may leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep TREK data directories separate from Khoj indexed folders.
Exclude secrets-bearing files from Khoj indexing rules.
Rotate any API keys or MFA secrets already stored in TREK if sharing occurred.
Review outbound search-provider settings in Khoj and disable them for sensitive notes.
requires-engineering: enforce per-app filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to mutable local resources: Khoj has shared index state across clients and TREK writes to travel.db, uploads, and logs. TREK also uses real-time collaboration and MCP, so concurrent edits or overlapping writes can corrupt shared artifacts if they are pointed at the same directory or database. No locking is documented, so conflict risk is plausible in default self-hosted setups.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same filesystem path, file corruption or lost updates can occur.
IF TREK MCP actions and Khoj indexing run concurrently on shared files, stale reads or write races are possible.
mitigations: Place Khoj and TREK on separate volumes or directories.
Pause indexing while TREK performs bulk imports or uploads.
Enable backups for travel.db and Khoj index data.
Review any shared MCP endpoints for write access.
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional coordination across both apps.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface facts from notes, while TREK is a collaborative travel planner with AI and action-oriented data like reservations and budgets. If TREK consumes Khoj-generated text as authoritative, a bad retrieval can cascade into incorrect bookings, itinerary changes, or user-facing decisions. The interaction is inferred, but the blast radius is high enough to warrant high.
conditions: IF TREK uses Khoj output as a source of truth without verification, incorrect facts can propagate into plans.
IF either agent auto-generates user-facing travel actions from the other's text, errors can cascade into real-world mistakes.
mitigations: Require human review before TREK acts on Khoj-derived facts.
Mark Khoj outputs as untrusted unless backed by source links.
Add validation checks for dates, prices, and reservation numbers.
Limit automatic action-taking in TREK for imported text.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while TREK handles reservations, country visit history, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. Both are self-hosted/open-source, but TREK also uses external APIs and allowlisted egress, so compliance gaps can arise if sensitive travel or identity data is routed through non-approved services. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF EU personal data from TREK is sent to external map or OIDC services without a DPA, compliance exposure exists.
IF Khoj indexes regulated notes and TREK stores matching identity data in the same environment, retention and access controls may diverge.
mitigations: Inventory which TREK APIs receive personal data.
Disable external providers for regulated notes in Khoj.
Document retention periods for travel.db and indexed notes.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive datasets by workspace.
requires-engineering: add residency and DPA enforcement for outbound services.
